scope.current_boundary: Read axes, coordinates, signs, stationary motion, direction, constant velocity and changing motion on displacement-time and velocity-time graphs. Determine velocity using the gradient of a displacement-time graph (straight line and tangent to curve). Determine acceleration using the gradient of a velocity-time graph (straight line and tangent to curve). Do not calculate areas under velocity-time graphs or use constant-acceleration equations.
scope.previous_boundary_used: Acceleration and describing changing motion provided the prior meanings of velocity, acceleration, direction and units.
scope.next_boundary_checked: Area and constructing motion graphs, including determining displacement from the area under a velocity-time graph and constructing motion graphs.

question_patterns_used.name: Graph interpretation
question_patterns_used.lesson_response: Teach axes, coordinates, signs, stationary intervals, direction and graph-type distinction before any numerical graph method.

question_patterns_used.name: Comparison
question_patterns_used.lesson_response: Compare horizontal sections and axis crossings on displacement-time and velocity-time graphs in a dedicated table.

question_patterns_used.name: Explanation
question_patterns_used.lesson_response: Require an explicit sign-based reason for a claimed direction reversal and repair the zero-velocity misconception.

questions_visited.why_selected: Shows the need to distinguish signed regions on a velocity-time graph from a simple visual total.
questions_visited.assessed_demand: Choose the signed relationship represented by regions above and below the velocity axis.
questions_visited.reasoning_route: Read whether each region is above or below zero before deciding how the graph information combines.
questions_visited.misconception_or_distractor: Treating every region as positive because it has a positive geometric area.
lesson_sections_informed: Read the axes before you describe the motion
Velocity-time graphs show velocity at each instant

questions_visited.why_selected: Requires matching a qualitative trace to a physical motion description rather than using numbers.
questions_visited.assessed_demand: Identify which graph could represent changing acceleration and velocity in a falling context.
questions_visited.reasoning_route: Link a graph's changing or constant vertical value to a stated physical quantity.
questions_visited.misconception_or_distractor: Assuming identical-looking graph shapes always represent the same physical quantity.
lesson_sections_informed: Read the axes before you describe the motion
Do not mix up the two graph types

questions_visited.why_selected: Compares different velocity-time traces with the same endpoints and duration.
questions_visited.assessed_demand: Select the car that reaches the shared final velocity in the shortest distance.
questions_visited.reasoning_route: Compare the information represented by the traces, not merely their final velocity and time.
questions_visited.misconception_or_distractor: Concluding that equal final velocity and time force equal motion throughout.
lesson_sections_informed: Velocity-time graphs show velocity at each instant
